newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-DEBUTANT NAZIR TAKES WICKET WITH FOURTH BALL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DEBUTANT NAZIR TAKES WICKET WITH FOURTH BALL.

text.p: Pakistan fast bowler Shahid Nazir made a flying start to his test career by capturing a wicket with his fourth ball against Zimbabwe on Thursday.
The 19-year-old seamer trapped Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell leg before for eight as the touring team reached 106 for two by lunch on the opening day of the first test after winning the toss.
Pakistani captain Wasim Akram made the initial breakthrough, removing opener Mark Dekker lbw for 14 with the total 33, before Nazir struck eight runs later.
Third-wicket pair Grant Flower and David Houghton repaired the early damage on a grassless, straw-coloured pitch, making 37 each before the interval.
Houghton, a century-maker in Zimbabwe's opening three-day match at Sahiwal, batted attractively, twice lifting off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq for six, while Flower struck five fours.

Apart from Nazir, Pakistan included another test debutant in middle-order batsman Azam Khan, but left out 16-year-old all-rounder Shahid Afridi, who broke the record for the fastest one-day international century in Nairobi last month.
Pakistan - Aamir Sohail, Saeed Anwar, Ijaz Ahmed, Salim Malik, Shadab Kabir, Azam Khan, Wasim Akram (captain), Moin Khan, Waqar Younis, Saqlain Mushtaq, Shahid Nazir.
Zimbabwe - Grant Flower, Mark Dekker, Alistair Campbell (captain), David Houghton, Andy Flower, Craig Wishart, Guy Whittall, Paul Strang, Andrew Whittall, Bryan Strang, Henry Olongo.
